original_value: Traffic collisions between kangaroos and motorists are on the rise on Australian roads. According to a recent report, it was estimated that there were more than 20,000 kangaroo vehicle collisions that occurred only during the year 2015 in Australia. In this work, we are proposing a vehicle-based framework for kangaroo detection in urban and highway traffic environment that could be used for collision warning systems. Our proposed framework is based on region-based convolutional neural networks (RCNN). Given the scarcity of labeled data of kangaroos in traffic environments, we utilized our state-of-the-art data generation pipeline to generate 17,000 synthetic depth images of traffic scenes with kangaroo instances annotated in them. We trained our proposed RCNN-based framework on a subset of the generated synthetic depth images dataset. The proposed framework achieved a higher average precision (AP) score of 92% over all the testing synthetic depth image datasets. We compared our proposed framework against other baseline approaches and we outperformed it with more than 37% in AP score over all the testing datasets. Additionally, we evaluated the generalization performance of the proposed framework on real live data and we achieved a resilient detection accuracy without any further fine-tuning of our proposed RCNN-based framework.

result.paraphrase: Traffic collisions involving kangaroos and motorists are increasing on Australian roads. A recent report estimated that more than 20,000 kangaroo-vehicle collisions occurred in Australia in 2015 alone. In this work, we propose a vehicle-based kangaroo detection framework for urban and highway traffic environments that could support collision warning systems. The framework is built on region-based convolutional neural networks (RCNN). Because labeled kangaroo data in traffic settings are scarce, we used our state-of-the-art data generation pipeline to create 17,000 synthetic depth images of traffic scenes with kangaroo instances annotated. We trained the proposed RCNN-based framework on a subset of this synthetic depth-image dataset. It achieved a higher average precision (AP) of 92% across all testing synthetic depth-image datasets. Compared with baseline approaches, it outperformed them by more than 37% in AP across all testing datasets. We also evaluated its generalization on real live data and obtained resilient detection accuracy without any further fine-tuning of the proposed RCNN-based framework.
